text: Not every database here is SQL Server. The plant floor's sensor system writes into iot_sensor_logs on a MongoDB server, brennan-mongo-01, that's never had a real DBA's attention -- until now.

First connection reveals the real problem: no authentication at all, not misconfigured, just never turned on. Anyone on the network already had full read and write access to every sensor reading this plant has collected.
Access control comes first, before backups, before monitoring -- a backup strategy means very little on a database anyone can already read or change directly.

With authorization enabled, a scoped application user replaces open access, and nightly mongodump backups with real retention give this database the same protection BrennanERP already has -- verified with an actual restore.
Same DBA discipline, different platform, now actually applied. Next: the first real test of BrennanAG itself, and what it finds.
